title: Answers to Political Questions: The Palestinian and Syrian Settlement Talks with the Jewish Entity - American Influence in Ukraine - America's Serious Orientation towards Africa - America's Insistence on Holding the Iraqi Elections on Schedule
text:
Answers to Political Questions

- The Palestinian and Syrian settlement talks with the Jewish entity

- American influence in Ukraine

- America's serious orientation towards Africa

- America's insistence on holding the Iraqi elections on schedule

1 - Recently, talk has begun to accelerate about settlements of the Palestinian-Israeli conflict and the Syrian-Israeli conflict, and this talk has become mixed with talk about the unilateral withdrawal from Gaza. This talk has intersected with press and semi-official talk in Egypt and Israel about plans drawn up for the solution, and that they are in the stage of study and discussion behind the scenes.

So is there any truth to this talk? Is there seriousness among the influential parties about entering negotiations along the lines of the Egyptian-Israeli Camp David agreement and the Jordanian-Israeli Wadi Araba agreement? Then what is the expected solution if there is some truth to it, or is this talk like the earlier talk which used to be stirred up and then subside without any result?

Answer:

What is most likely is that there is a serious orientation towards entering Palestinian and Syrian settlement talks with (Israel) during Bush's new term.

What makes this matter most likely are the following indicators:

First: America's orientation with regard to the Middle East crisis was that the settlement of the Palestinian negotiation with the Jewish entity should not be concluded except after the settlement of the negotiation with Syria, or in conjunction with it. Therefore, when Clinton tried hard to reach a negotiated solution of the Palestinian issue with the Jews, he likewise began bringing the Syrian and Israeli parties together. Both the Palestinian negotiating party and the Syrian negotiating party were ready to recognise the Jewish entity in Palestine before 67, ready to guarantee its security, preserve its borders and normalise completely with it, on condition that it withdraw from the lands occupied after 67. But Israeli public opinion and many influential Jewish politicians refused to accept withdrawing from the lands occupied in 1967 in exchange for the recognition of their ownership of Palestine 48 and complete normalisation with them; rather, they want their ownership of Palestine 48 and also positions in Palestine 67 and in the Golan occupied in 1967. As for the Palestinian and Syrian side, Arafat and Hafez Assad were convinced that the utmost of their capacity for oppression and pressure was to force the Palestinians and the Syrians to accept giving up Palestine 48, and no more.

Therefore the negotiations stopped and did not reach a result.

Second: after the era of Clinton and the coming of Bush, there was 11 September, and Bush's priority was the savage, criminal aggression against Afghanistan and Iraq. Therefore there were no serious actions from him in managing the Middle East crisis, and all that took place, the coming and going of envoys, was only public relations to facilitate Bush's criminal acts in Afghanistan and Iraq. Even the Greater Middle East project which Bush announced was likewise so, and the serious beginning of its implementation was not intended in Bush's first term.

Third: after Bush's success in his second term, the following happened:

1 - A new Palestinian leadership headed by Mahmoud Abbas, who is known to be against the militarisation of the Intifada. Today, 15/12/2004, he requested in a statement that the people of Palestine end the armed Intifada, and Bush praised him for that. His experience in the presidency of the Palestinian cabinet satisfies America and the Jews, and of course Europe. He is the author of the famous statement that he (will put an end to the sufferings of the Jewish people!). So his readiness to give up more than Palestine 48 is a matter beyond doubt.

Fourth: the statement of Terje Larsen (in month 11) at a press conference following his talks in Damascus with Assad and the Syrian Foreign Minister Farouk al-Sharaa, that the Syrian President informed him that (his hand is extended to the Israelis and that he is ready to go to the negotiating table without preconditions).

And the statement of the spokesman of the Egyptian presidency, Magued Abdel Fattah, following Mubarak's meeting with Assad in Sharm el-Sheikh, which lasted nearly two hours, his statement that Syria expressed its readiness to begin direct negotiations with Israel without preconditions and that Syria no longer holds to the Rabin deposit.

All of this reflects a new orientation in the current Syrian leadership regarding the negotiations, since Syria used to insist that any negotiation with the Jews begin from this point, not begin from zero. And Sharon used to refuse that.

The Syrian President's acceptance of negotiating from zero means, in reality, readiness to give up parts of the Golan. And this reality is not changed by the Syrian Information Minister's playing with words when he said that our agreement to negotiate without preconditions does not mean beginning from zero, because we consider negotiations from the point they reached not a precondition but rather the natural course of things!

Syria had paved the way for this matter when it issued, in the name of the parties allied with it and under its wing in the (National Progressive Front), a decision cancelling the paragraph contained in the Front's charter which stipulates (no peace and no negotiation with the Zionist state).

The president of the Zionist entity welcomed the Syrian President's extended hand and said it is not right that we do not respond. Likewise, the head of the Israeli intelligence mission (Aharon Zeevi) said on 1/12 that the (messages and hints) issued from Damascus must not be ignored. And Sharon said: I am ready to negotiate with Syria, but with conditions! That is, Syria gave up the conditions, and the state of the Jews is the one that sets the conditions. Nevertheless, this is not so much a refusal from Sharon as blackmail of Syria, according to the habit of the Jews in negotiating with the Arabs.

Fifth: the American President Bush stated on 4/12 that the establishment of a Palestinian state to live in peace and security with Israel will be among the priorities of his administration during his second term of presidency. He said that during a press conference he held after talks he conducted with Musharraf.

Likewise, it was reported that Condoleezza Rice, the appointed Secretary of State of the new American administration, said: (The American administration is in the process of raising the level of its involvement in the Middle East region and focusing on the peace process and the Palestinian elections scheduled for the ninth of next month).

And also what The New York Times reported on 2/12/2004 about James Baker, the Secretary of State of America in the era of Bush the father, that he addressed a call to the current President Bush the son, calling him to more engagement in the peace process in the Middle East.

These indicators point to the likelihood of the seriousness of America's gathering of the Palestinian, Syrian and Israeli parties in settlement negotiations, and that the negotiations on the Palestinian and Syrian tracks will be in conjunction or close together, according to the agenda that America draws up for the negotiating parties.

Here we have not mentioned the position of the European Union, especially Britain and France, because the European party was not an obstacle in the negotiations. Added to that, it is unable to move the negotiating process without America's agreement; indeed, what is noticed is that it picks up the projects that America puts forward and then sets off from them, as happened with the Road Map and the disengagement plan, and then tries, through proceeding with them, to achieve its interests individually or collectively.

As for what the expected solution is, it is declared, and it suffices to point to it:

A - With regard to the West Bank and the Strip:

* It is the Road Map which, if implemented, gives the Authority 42% of the West Bank and the Strip, called a state without full sovereignty and semi-demilitarised.

* And it has shrunk to the Gaza Strip and a little of the West Bank, all of which does not exceed 25% of the West Bank and the Strip.

* And finally Bush defined it in the letter of guarantees which he sent to Sharon last April:

1 - Dropping the right of return of the Palestinian refugees in order to preserve the Jewish character of the state of the Jews.

2 - Keeping the main Jewish settlements in the West Bank in the hands of the Jewish state.

3 - Not returning to the 1967 borders, including Jerusalem, but rather taking into account the facts on the ground.

America claimed that these foundations do not contradict the Road Map nor the international resolutions such as Resolution 242, because in its English text it did not stipulate the return of the lands occupied in 1967 but rather the return of lands.

B - With regard to the Golan:

* The Syrian President's statement about negotiating without preconditions, that is, without returning to the point the previous negotiations reached, means that Syria is ready to accept that part of the Golan remain under Israeli sovereignty.

These are America's plans, and these are the men of government in Syria and the men of the Authority. Their acceptance of giving up parts of what was occupied in 1967 is not surprising. As long as they have given up Palestine 1948, and have recognised, and have the readiness to recognise, the Jewish entity in Palestine 1948 and to give it up finally, then whoever is in this state, it will not be strange for him to give up parts of what was occupied in 1967. For whoever concedes once concedes many times, and whoever concedes a metre concedes kilometres.

Whoever is debased finds debasement easy to bear; a wound brings no pain to the dead.

These are the rulers, but they do not represent the Muslims, nor do they speak in their name, nor do they possess the right to give up the land of Islam and the Muslims. The Muslims will not accept any substitute for all of Palestine and all of the Golan, and they will not accept recognition of the Jewish entity even on a single span of the land of the Muslims. Palestine will return completely to Dar al-Islam, and the Jewish entity will be eliminated, by the permission of Allah. The sincere believers will bring that about, for the fighting of the Jews and victory over them is coming without doubt, by the permission of Allah. And those who recognise the Jewish entity, who negotiate with them and surrender to them, will obtain nothing but disgrace in this world and painful punishment from the State of the Khilafah, which will be established by the permission of Allah, this besides the painful torment in the Hereafter: “And the punishment of Allah is greater, if only they knew.”

2 - The second round of the Ukrainian elections is scheduled to be repeated on 26/12/2004, and the success of the opposition leader in it is expected. So can it be said that the popular opposition movement in Ukraine is on the same steps that the popular opposition in Georgia followed, and that it will lead to the entry of American influence into Ukraine and its final distancing from Russia?

Answer: Whoever follows the question of Ukraine finds that it differs from the question of Georgia. In Georgia, American influence had entered it beforehand, and it was among the fastest of the republics of the Soviet Union to leave Russia's influence. Shevardnadze brought the Americans into the country and concluded military and economic agreements with them. Then, when he tried to have a margin of movement, so as to move towards Russia and America, that is, to hold the stick from the middle or close to the middle, America moved its men, headed by its agent Saakashvili, who reached power by way of his (velvet) revolution, as he called it, and forced Shevardnadze to give up power.

As for Ukraine, it is closely connected with Russia and an important ally of it, besides the existence of Ukrainians who consider themselves as if they were Russians; they speak Russian and a large proportion of them descend from Russian origins, especially those living in eastern Ukraine. Therefore it is not easy for America to dominate Ukraine as it did in Georgia.

This is despite America's multiple attempts to introduce institutions of its own into Ukraine, directly or indirectly. In the capital Kyiv there is a branch of the institute of the (Freedom House) union, which is run in America by James Woolsey, who was formerly director of the Central Intelligence. The (Freedom House) union contributed greatly to the toppling of the Serbian President (Milosevic) by way of the leader of the Serbian students (Aleksandar Maric), and the latter tried to enter Ukraine during the electoral campaign for the Ukrainian presidency but could not obtain an entry visa. (Freedom House) likewise contributed to the popular movement in Georgia.

Despite all the efforts exerted by America in Ukraine, its ability to dominate Ukraine and distance it from Russia is not easy, because of Russia's roots in Ukraine and because of Ukraine's importance to Russia. It is a relatively large country (48 million people) and almost an extension of Russia demographically and geographically, and no barriers separate it from Russia proper. It is not like Georgia, the small country (5.5 million), which is separated from Russia by the Islamic regions in the Caucasus.

For all of that:

The prior existence of American influence in Georgia before the popular movement, Georgia's distancing from Russia a short time after the dissolution of the former Soviet Union, its smallness and its lack of great importance to Russia; whereas Ukraine is attached to Russia and an extension of it in population and geography, especially from the east, with its large size and its importance to Russia, and American influence had not entered it before the current popular movement: all of that makes the question of Ukraine differ from Georgia. And the fact that America was able to win the battle in Georgia, deal Putin a harsh blow there and drive Russian influence out of Georgia, the fact that it succeeded in that does not make it succeed with a like success in Ukraine.

The effective role of Russian influence in Ukraine against the popular movement led by (Yushchenko) was clear. Russia obstructed several attempts by the opposition to pass the repetition of the elections or the inauguration of Yushchenko, and this obstruction continued, and it was able to extract from the Ukrainian parliament an amendment of the constitution limiting the powers of the President of the Republic, who is expected to be Yushchenko after the repeated elections.

On 8/12/2004 parliament voted successfully on amending the constitution to reduce the powers of the President. Among them was the transfer of the power of appointing to the senior posts from the President to parliament, and parliament's ratification was made a condition for appointing the Prime Minister and the ministers of defence and foreign affairs, which had been exclusively the President's before the amendment. This was done despite the opposition of Yushchenko and his followers, and all of it was done by Russia and its followers in Ukraine, and Yushchenko was forced to agree to this reduction against his will.

Russia likewise obstructed beforehand the meeting of the Supreme Court; then, when it met on 4/12, Russia influenced it to push the repetition of the second round as far away as possible, so it set it for 26/12/2004, so that it could complete the amendment of the constitution and so that the momentum of the opposition would lessen, which wanted to settle matters in its favour quickly, as we saw in the first days after the elections when (Yulia Tymoshenko), one of the leaders of the opposition, called out to Yushchenko to take the constitutional oath as President of the Republic. So delaying the settlement to 26/12 is against the wishes of the opposition, because it lessens its momentum. This was done under Russia's influence before the court convened on 4/12, as there was suddenly announced a lightning visit made by the outgoing Ukrainian President to Moscow on 2/12, during which he met Putin and then returned directly to Kyiv, and two days after that the court convened.

From the foregoing it becomes clear that it is not easy for an American solution to be found in Ukraine that Russia does not agree to, and even if America succeeded in bringing one of its men to power without Russia's agreement, Russia would soon topple him anew. Russia is able not only to obstruct any American solution by political means but also by threats. It notified Interpol of criminal cases against the mentioned Yulia, and her name remained on Interpol's lists until 8/12, when parliament approved the amendments. Then Yulia learned the strength of Russia's influence, so she softened her tone and stated, saying: (It is necessary to take Russian interests in Ukraine into account), then added, affirming that relations between the two countries will be warmer in the event of Yushchenko's victory, and expressed her hope that the file of the Russian public prosecution's demand for her arrest through Interpol would be closed. This is in addition to what some news reports carried, that Yushchenko's current illness is poisoning and that Russia or its followers may have a connection to it.

In conclusion, America's domination of Ukraine and its distancing from Russia is not easy for America as it was in Georgia.

There is no doubt that America realises that, and here a question appears: then what is the aim of this great effort exerted by America in moving the opposition with this momentum? To answer this question we say: America realises that it will not be able to take Ukraine to its side and distance it from Russia completely as it did in Georgia, but it wanted to create a hotbed of tension in the flank of Russia and the flank of Europe as well, especially after the accession of the states of Eastern Europe to the European Union and the European Union's approach to Ukraine; that is, it wanted to create a new Yugoslavia there. Thus it would have struck two birds with one stone: it creates a problem for Europe with which it frightens it and occupies it, namely the separation of eastern Ukraine, or at least its demand for self-rule, and the destabilisation of the situation in Ukraine. At the same time it creates a problem for Russia, because Russia will not let Ukraine slip from its hand, especially as it has strong influence in eastern Ukraine, where the nerve of Ukraine's industrial and economic life lies. Thus America would have created in the flank of Russia and Europe a strong card of pressure and bargaining that limits Europe's and Russia's disturbance of America regarding its projects in the region, whether that be in the Middle East or in Central Asia.

This is clear from America's strong role in moving the events of Ukraine, the European role that eases the events for fear of the situation worsening, and the Russian role resisting the American role.

As for the American role moving the events, the spring of the popular movement is Yushchenko, or (Yushchenka) as it is pronounced in Ukrainian, and he is known to be America's man in Ukraine. He was prepared by way of the National Democratic Institute, which is headed by Madeleine Albright, the former American Secretary of State, and some sources have mentioned that Kateryna, Yushchenko's wife, used to work with the American State Department. Madeleine Albright is also the one who prepared Yushchenka's electoral campaign and carefully chose a director for it, namely the head of the American Open Society association in Ukraine, and this is an organisation funded by the Jewish American billionaire (George Soros), and it had a prominent role in the events of Georgia.

Thus it can be said that the opposition movement was an American manufacture.

As for the European role, what is noticed is that Europe tried from the beginning to mend the rift between the opposition and the government in Ukraine, and tried to come out with a solution to the crisis as quickly as possible before the situation worsened, especially when the eastern regions announced their intention to separate or to obtain self-rule through a popular vote, and the supporters of Viktor Yanukovych, the officially declared winner of the elections and the current Prime Minister of Ukraine, came out into the streets in demonstrations supporting him as a reaction to the demonstrations supporting Yushchenko. Europe hastened to send the mediators, namely the Lithuanian President Valdas Adamkus, the Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski, the High Representative for Foreign Policy of the European Union Javier Solana and the Secretary General of the Organisation for Security and Co-operation in Europe Jan Kubis. They held lengthy meetings, three times, with representatives of the Ukrainian government in the presence of the Speaker of the Russian Duma, Boris Gryzlov. This indicates Europe's keenness to end the crisis as quickly as possible without allowing it to worsen, so it hastened, as soon as the crisis erupted, to send the mediators to Kyiv. That goes back to the demographic structure of Ukraine, wide areas of which, such as Crimea, belonged to Russia (after Russia usurped it from the Ottoman State) and were ceded to Ukraine, in addition to the Ukrainians of Russian origin living in eastern Ukraine, this besides the division of the Ukrainian people between the two churches, the Orthodox in the east and the Catholic in the west of Ukraine. This sum of data gives the opportune chance for a new Yugoslavia in Europe, that is, the tearing apart of Ukraine as Yugoslavia was torn apart, and this is exactly what Europe fears most intensely.

As for the resisting Russian role, it took several forms. At the beginning Putin called Viktor Yanukovych congratulating him on his success in the elections and his winning of the presidency of the state as successor to the outgoing Kuchma; then he went back and retreated after the increase of the popular opposition pressures demanding the repetition of the second electoral round because of the fraud. Then Russia began to focus on the unconstitutionality of repeating the second stage, and rather on repeating the elections from their beginnings, and that was in agreement with Kuchma, according to his statements during the crisis, to prolong the period of settlement so that it would psychologically affect the momentum of the opposition. After that it resorted to opening criminal files on the poles of the opposition, beginning with the case of (Yulia Tymoshenko); then it resorted to pressure and the threat of moving eastern Ukraine, which is loyal to it, to influence the course of events. It was clear that Russia did not want their movement to reach separation, which would achieve America's purposes; rather, what was intended was to create a popular reaction counter to the opposition, to create a balance between the two popular movements, in order to return matters to a middle solution that calms them and returns them to what they were, so as to block the way before America's plans. Therefore government parties (the outgoing President Kuchma and the Speaker of parliament) met with them, and they stated at the end of the meeting that their aim in that was only political pressure to end the protests by the opposition and in support of their candidate Viktor Yanukovych. This might have appeared to the public as if it were a retreat by the parties loyal to the government, but the matter in reality was the defusing of the crisis, which would have led to a civil war that would have led to the partition of Ukraine. This civil war would have occupied Russia as well as Europe, because the fire would be burning not only in the courtyard of their house but in the very heart of their home. That civil war would have been the golden opportunity for America to complete its plans in Central Asia and the Caucasus as well as Eastern Europe. It would also be an occupation for Europe, allowing America to proceed forward with its projects, whether in Eastern Europe or in the whole world, and it would also be a card of pressure on Europe to go along with America completely in its international policies, such as those relating to Iraq for example. And America would thereby show Europe, which aims to rid itself of American hegemony by bringing about a unified European constitution and a European military general staff and a European military intervention force, it would show it how weak and incapable it is, even of dealing with its own problems inside Europe, so it should not aspire to an international role with which it struggles against the United States of America.

Therefore the exchange of accusations between Russia and the European Union regarding Ukraine was only to throw dust in the eyes, and so that Europe would appear as a party contrary to Russia, which would give it a greater opportunity to manoeuvre, although they both strive for the same aim. It also shows the dangers that could befall the Ukrainian people in the event of a division in Ukraine and the firing of the first bullet. Therefore we find that as soon as the parliament's decision was announced, the Ukrainian politicians hastened to affirm a unified Ukraine and that it is capable of solving its problems, as the Speaker of parliament Volodymyr Lytvyn said that the parliament's success in approving the new legislation is a step on the road of reconciliation and proves that Ukraine is unified and not divisible.

Therefore it can be said that America did not aspire to take Ukraine and distance it from Russia finally as in Georgia; rather, it wanted to create a hotbed of tension in Ukraine and the escalation of the crisis between the opposition, led by its agent Yushchenka, which would push eastern Ukraine to a counter-reaction leading the country to total or partial partition, and this worries Russia and Europe and occupies them with a danger knocking on their door. At the same time it can be said that Europe and Russia were able to ease the crisis to some extent by introducing the amendments to the constitution and reducing the powers of the President of the Republic, such that Yushchenka's success as head of state would have reduced powers balanced with the powers of parliament and the powers of the Prime Minister, who will in this case be from Russia's supporters, and consequently matters in Ukraine can be calmed and not reach a state of crisis.

But what can likewise be said is that Ukraine has been placed, from this day onwards, on the road of crisis. For America will not be content with matters calming down through a solution of (no victor and no vanquished); rather, it will return and detonate the situation whenever it finds the circumstances opportune and whenever it wants to pressure Russia and Europe and occupy them with the danger creeping into the very heart of their home, for the sake of facilitating the implementation of America's plans in the region.

Thus it becomes clear that the reality of the two questions (Georgia and Ukraine) is different, and the aim of America's plans in them is likewise different.

3 - The day of 31/12/2004 is the day on which the two parties (the Sudanese government and the rebels in the south led by Garang) pledged to complete the implementation of the agreement ending the civil war in the south. This pledge was signed before the Security Council, which convened in Nairobi on 19/11/2004 instead of convening at its permanent headquarters in New York. So does this mean that the matter of Sudan is of such importance that the Security Council moves to convene in Africa, and that a delegate of the Council could not be sent instead of its moving in its entirety? Or are there other purposes for the convening of the Security Council?

Answer: As for the importance of Sudan, yes, it is important. It was the focus of the West's attention throughout the last century, since the British influence in it and its linking to Egypt. Then, when it separated from Egypt, the English influence kept going away from it and returning, until American influence settled in it in the era of Nimeiry and the era of al-Bashir. And Europe (Britain and France) is still trying to penetrate it, as was noticed in the exploitation of the Darfur issue recently, and it is still trying to have an entry into Sudan. Accordingly, in terms of importance, Sudan is important and it is the focus of the attention of the major players in international politics.

However, if the matter related only to Sudan, that would not have called for the Security Council to move to Nairobi to discuss this subject; rather, a delegate of the Council, or an American and Europe, would have come, as happened before that.

But whoever follows the subject sees that the United States, after Bush's success in his second term, has begun to give its attention seriously to Africa, after the events of Afghanistan and Iraq occupied it, that is the United States, for most of Bush's first term.

From here came the meeting of the Security Council in Africa, as an indication of the serious orientation of the United States towards Africa. As for the evidence of that, it is:

1 - The one who proposed and insisted that the Security Council be held in Nairobi is the president of the Security Council in the month of November 2004, who is the delegate of the United States of America (John Danforth).

2 - The Security Council that convened in Nairobi did not discuss the question of Sudan only; rather, it touched on the Great Lakes region with its fifteen states. And it gave importance to the summit conference of these states, which was held in Dar es Salaam and attended by the presidents of those states, who signed a declaration of peace between them and then decided to hold their second conference in June 2005 in Nairobi. The summit conference of the Great Lakes states took many times over the Security Council's time compared with what the Sudan issue took; indeed, the question of Sudan had a clearly defined (agenda), for most of the items had been discussed and agreed upon between the government of Sudan and Garang's movement, and their attendance was for the signing and the protocol meeting.

Accordingly, it can be said that America has decided, now in Bush's second term, has decided to escalate its campaign in the direction of Africa, not Sudan only but the entire Great Lakes region with its fifteen states, along two parallel lines: the first, consolidating its three agents in that region (Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi), and the second, setting off from these three to the rest of the Great Lakes states. Consequently the line of American depth in Africa is completed: from the east, Eritrea, Ethiopia and Sudan (especially its south), and to the middle of Africa in the Great Lakes states, then Côte d'Ivoire in the west, where the effective American role moving the events of Côte d'Ivoire has become clear with the beginning of Bush's second term. This confirms the previous statement that America decided to escalate its campaign in the direction of Africa since the beginning of Bush's second term, and this matter is no longer hidden. The Ivorian President (Gbagbo) moved, relying on America to back him, but he exceeded the permitted limit and bombed the French army stationed there as an international force to separate the resistance in the north (with a Muslim majority) from the army of the government of Côte d'Ivoire. This mistake of his caused embarrassment for America, so it could not back him. France exploited this situation and moved its agents in Africa (and Britain helped it with its agents as well), as a meeting of the African Union was held in Abuja and expressed its support for the French draft resolution which was to be discussed in the Security Council at a later time, where it was approved, including an arms embargo on Côte d'Ivoire for a period of (13) months.

Were it not for the mistake of the President of Côte d'Ivoire in bombing the French army there, the French presence in Côte d'Ivoire would have ended completely and American influence would have settled in it without contest. It was clear to the men of politics that Côte d'Ivoire's move against France was driven by America, and this is what the director of the Centre for Geopolitical Studies in Paris stated, saying: (The Ivorian President is waging a proxy war on France and turning Côte d'Ivoire into an arena for settling accounts with the United States, for the latter to take possession of Côte d'Ivoire).

It is expected that the events will be set in motion again by the United States, in more suitable circumstances and with more studied arrangements with the President of Côte d'Ivoire (Gbagbo), because the United States will not leave Côte d'Ivoire, since it has a strategic location on the Atlantic coast, which means that it will be a spearhead that America supports for the sake of penetrating deeply into Africa. If it fell into its hand completely, and the influence of France (Europe) in it ended, it would be a launching point for America from West Africa, like Ethiopia and Eritrea in the east, in addition to southern Sudan, passing through Central Africa in the Great Lakes region, especially Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi.

In conclusion, the meeting of the Security Council in Nairobi is an indication of the United States' serious interest in Africa and in taking possession of it.

4 - What is this strange insistence of the American administration and the Iraqi government on holding the elections at the end of next month, despite the palpable lack of security stability in Iraq and despite the declared boycott by influential sectors in Iraq such as the Association of Muslim Scholars? And can any elections boycotted by an important part of Iraq achieve the results that America claims it wants from them, in terms of their representing the people?

Answer: America is playing a malicious and dangerous game in Iraq. It has realised that all the force, tyranny and savage oppression it has expended have not been able to extinguish or lessen Iraq's resistance to America, because they view it as a Kafir colonialist state occupying the country, and they view the interim Iraqi government as an agent government, an American manufacture.

It appears that America saw that the people of Iraq confronting one another would relieve it of the trouble of fighting, and would make the people of Iraq view it as their rescuer from the evils of internal fighting when it occurs.

For this reason it insisted on the elections taking place, to bring about a government that appears (legitimate) because it comes by way of elections, and in this case the Shia will have predominated in it and an important part of the Sunnis will be outside it, and keeping security becomes the responsibility of the Shia in confrontation with the Sunnis. This will lighten the burden on the occupation forces, and they will come to watch the situation from afar, after the confrontation had been between them and the people of Iraq, that is, a confrontation between the occupier and those under occupation; so the picture is overturned into a confrontation between those under occupation.

What indicates that America wants to transfer the confrontation from occupation forces and those under occupation to a confrontation among those under occupation themselves, a (legitimate, elected) government and those who rebel against it, are the following indicators:

1 - The security situation in Iraq is unstable, and this is a palpable matter, and it is clear in what is called the Sunni triangle; that is, even if they did not boycott the elections, they cannot go to them safely, nor can they carry out electoral campaigning in the known manner.

2 - The influential opinion in the Sunni areas is to boycott the elections, because of their conviction that the elections have no value as long as the occupier is present in Iraq, and this is what the Association of Muslim Scholars declares. Even those from these areas who agree to the elections under the occupation tried to have them postponed and requested that.

3 - The predominant opinion in the Shia areas is agreement to the elections, and indeed strong enthusiasm for them and intensive mobilisation for them, and this is what the Shia Marja'iyya in Najaf has declared, and this is what those areas are witnessing of complete campaigning and preparation for them, to the degree of calling the Iraqi Shia outside the country, such as those in Iran, to return to attend these elections, and the news has carried the existence of a striking movement of entry from the direction of Iran.

All these factors will make the electoral results produce a dangerous division and a great rift between the Muslims in Iraq, Sunni and Shia, apart from the Kurdish region, which has its own well-known character.

4 - Added to that are the statements of the American officials themselves expecting a civil war in Iraq after the holding of the elections, such as the statement of the American Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Myers about the expectation of civil war.

From the foregoing it becomes clear that America's insistence on holding the elections on schedule, despite the great and clear divergence between the opinion of the Shia and the Sunnis about the elections, throwing to the wall even the requests to postpone the holding of the elections submitted by political forces known for their loyalty to America and for their agreement to the elections under the occupation, since they did not request their cancellation but their postponement for a few months so that the situation would stabilise, and to save their face before the Muslims; nevertheless, America did not take these requests for postponement into account, but insisted on holding them on time despite its officials' expectation that a civil war would occur after them: from all of that, the most likely is what we said at the beginning of the answer, that America wants by this insistence to make the confrontation after the elections between the (legitimate) government with a Muslim Shia majority and the Muslim Sunni resistance, instead of the confrontation being between the Muslims (Sunni and Shia) and the occupiers, and thereby the burden on America and the other occupation forces is lightened.

Accordingly, these elections, besides their violation of the Sharia because they are under the occupation, carry the danger of internal fighting instead of fighting the occupation forces.

3rd Dhul Qi'dah 1425 AH
